title: Physical education
description: Progressive pathways for swimming, skating, martial arts as fitness and discipline, general exercise, cycling, running and hiking. Activities adapt to age, ability and medical needs; swimming always needs a qualified teacher or lifeguarded pool, and martial arts never means street fighting.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Happy in the water
items.summary: Splash, blow bubbles and get your face wet with a grown-up right next to you.
steps: 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 A grown-up stays in the water, within arm's reach.
💦 Splash with your hands.
🫧 Blow bubbles on the water like a fish.
👀 Put your face in for a moment, then up.
🐸 Hop like a frog in shallow water.
🙌 Get out when you feel cold or tired.

safety.notes: An adult in the water within arm's reach at all times. Only in a lifeguarded shallow pool or with an adult in a bath. Never leave a child near water, even for a moment.

basic.description: Blow bubbles and splash in the bath with an adult beside you.

better.description: Play water games in a lifeguarded shallow pool with an adult.

materials: swimming lessons with a qualified teacher
advanced.description: Join beginner lessons with a qualified swimming teacher.

plastic cups and clean empty bottles

items.adultNote: Drowning is fast and silent. Supervise with full attention, no phones. Adapt to your child's ability. If your child has a medical condition, injury or disability, check with a doctor or physiotherapist before starting.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Water safety rules
items.summary: Water is fun but it can be dangerous. Learn the rules that keep you safe.
steps: 🙋 Always ask a grown-up before going near water.
👀 Swim only where a grown-up or lifeguard is watching.
🚫 Never swim alone.
🚩 Look for flags and signs and do what they say.
🧊 Cold water takes your breath away. Get in slowly.
📣 See someone in trouble? Shout for help. Do not go in.

safety.notes: Knowledge lesson. Real water activities always need adult supervision.

sources.title: Water safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents

check.question: Can you swim on your own if nobody is watching?
check.explain: Right. Always swim where a grown-up or lifeguard is watching.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Starfish float
items.summary: Float on your back like a starfish. Floating helps you rest and stay safe in water.
steps: 🧑‍🏫 Your teacher holds you. Lie back in the water.
👀 Look up at the ceiling or sky.
⭐ Stretch arms and legs out like a starfish.
😮‍💨 Breathe slowly and relax.
🤲 Your teacher lets go a little when you are ready.
🧍 Try a front float too, then stand up safely.

safety.notes: Only with a qualified swimming teacher or lifeguard present, in water at a depth the teacher chooses. The family adult watches from the side or joins in as the teacher directs.

basic.description: Practise the starfish shape lying on the floor.

better.description: Practise with a float in a lifeguarded pool.

advanced.description: Learn floating with a qualified teacher.

items.title: Kick, pull, breathe: front crawl
items.summary: Learn kicking, arm pulls and side breathing to swim front crawl, then work towards 25 metres.
steps: Kick with straight legs from the hips, toes pointed.
Practise kicking holding the side or a float.
Add long arm pulls, one at a time.
Turn your head to the side to breathe, then back down and blow bubbles.
Put it together for a few metres, then rest.
Build up slowly towards 25 metres with your teacher.

safety.notes: In lessons with a qualified swimming teacher, or in a lifeguarded pool with an adult. Rest when tired.

basic.description: Practise arm movements and side breathing on dry land.

better.description: Practise in a lifeguarded pool with an adult.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Water survival skills
items.summary: Learn to float, tread water, signal for help and keep warm if you fall in.
steps: Float to Live: lean back, spread arms and legs, and float to catch your breath.
Tread water: slow circles with arms and legs to stay upright.
Signal for help: one arm up, wave and shout.
Cold water: stay calm for the first minute while your breathing settles, then float.
In clothes, practise floating and moving to the side with your teacher.
Learn how to exit the water safely at the side.

safety.notes: Survival skills are practised only in lessons with a qualified teacher in a lifeguarded pool. Never practise in open water.

basic.description: Learn the steps and practise the float and signal shapes on land.

better.description: Practise floating and treading water with a lifeguard watching.

advanced.description: Take a survival or water safety course with a qualified teacher.

substitutions.use: a school or community water safety session where available

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Reach or throw, don't go
items.summary: If someone is in trouble in water, never jump in. Shout for help, then reach or throw something that floats.
steps: Shout for help and call the emergency number. Tell a lifeguard if there is one.
Stay on land and lie or kneel down so you are not pulled in.
Reach with a stick, towel or clothing.
Throw something that floats: a ball, an empty bottle, a ring.
Practise throwing a rope or bottle to a target on dry ground.
Never go into the water to rescue someone. That is a job for trained lifeguards.

safety.notes: Practise only on dry land away from water, such as a garden or park, with an adult watching.

materials: empty plastic bottle with a little water
basic.description: Throw a bottle to a hoop or mark on the grass.

better.description: Practise throwing a rope to a partner standing on land.

advanced.description: Join a junior lifesaving course at a pool.

substitutions.use: a clean empty plastic bottle tied to a rope or long scarf

sources.title: Water safety
sources.publisher: Royal Society for the Prevention of Accidents

items.certificationNote: Rescue skills in water are taught only on accredited lifesaving courses. Children must never attempt in-water rescues.
items.adultNote: Reinforce: the first rule is your own safety. Many would-be rescuers drown.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Open water: rivers, lakes and sea
items.summary: Open water is very different from a pool. Learn about cold, currents and how to stay safe.
steps: Only swim at lifeguarded beaches, between the flags.
Cold water shock: enter slowly; if you fall in, float first to catch your breath.
Rip currents: do not swim against them. Float, raise a hand, swim parallel to the shore when you can.
Rivers and lakes hide deep water, weeds, cold and fast flows.
Always go with others and tell someone where you are going.
Never swim after drinking alcohol or at night.

safety.notes: Knowledge only. Open-water swimming needs a qualified coach, safety cover and appropriate equipment.

items.subject: swimming
items.title: Swim further: endurance and strokes
items.summary: Build stamina and try backstroke and breaststroke as well as front crawl.
steps: Warm up with easy lengths.
Try backstroke: on your back, long arms, steady kick.
Try breaststroke: pull, breathe, kick, glide.
Swim sets: for example 4 x 25 metres with rests.
Add a little more each week.
Cool down and stretch.

safety.notes: Train in a lifeguarded pool or with a club coach. Never swim alone.

items.subject: skating
items.title: Gear up and balance
items.summary: Put on your helmet and pads, then find your balance on wheels.
steps: Put on a helmet, wrist guards, elbow pads and knee pads.
Start on grass or carpet so the wheels do not roll much.
Stand with feet a little apart, knees bent, arms forward.
March on the spot, then take small duck steps.
Move to a flat, smooth, quiet area away from roads.
Look ahead, not at your feet.

safety.notes: Always wear a helmet and wrist guards. Adult supervision. Never skate on roads or slopes when learning. Sock gliding only on a clear floor away from stairs, glass doors and sharp corners.

basic.description: Practise balance and gliding in socks on a smooth floor.

better.description: Use second-hand skates with a well-fitting helmet and pads.

advanced.description: Take lessons at a rink with a qualified coach.

substitutions.use: sliding in socks on a smooth floor to learn balance
second-hand pads checked for fit and damage (a helmet must be undamaged and fit well)

items.subject: skating
items.title: Fall safely and stop
items.summary: Learn to fall safely and stop before you learn to go fast.
steps: Falling: bend knees, crouch low, fall forward onto knee pads, then wrist guards.
Practise falls on grass first.
Get up: kneel, put one foot flat, push up with hands on knee.
Stop with the heel brake: one foot forward, lift toes, press the heel.
Or a T-stop: drag the back skate behind at a right angle.
Practise skating forward and stopping on a line.

safety.notes: Full protective gear. Practise falls on grass. Adult supervision on a quiet, flat surface.

basic.description: Practise falling on grass and stopping at chalk lines.

better.description: Practise in a quiet car-free area.

advanced.description: Learn stops with a qualified coach.

substitutions.use: plastic cups or shoes as markers

items.subject: skating
items.title: Turns and manoeuvres
items.summary: Carve turns, weave cones and learn crossovers with control.
steps: Warm up skating forward and stopping.
Lean gently to turn; look where you want to go.
Weave through a line of cones.
Try a crossover turn slowly in a circle.
Learn to skate backwards with small C-shapes.
Only try tricks or ramps at a supervised skate park with full gear.

safety.notes: Full protective gear. Car-free area or rink. Ramps and tricks only at supervised parks.

basic.description: Weave through home-made markers.

better.description: Practise turns at a public rink.

advanced.description: Learn advanced skills with a qualified coach.

items.subject: martial-arts
items.title: Walk away and get help
items.summary: The first self-defence skill is staying calm, walking away and getting help.
steps: Notice when you feel unsafe. Trust that feeling.
Use a strong, calm voice: Stop. Leave me alone.
Keep your distance and walk away towards people.
Go to a trusted adult, a shop, school or a safe place.
Tell someone what happened.
Fighting is the very last thing, only to escape. Never start a fight.

safety.notes: Talking and role-play only. No contact.

check.question: Someone is trying to start a fight. What is the best first choice?
check.explain: Yes. Walking away and getting help is the strongest self-defence skill.

items.adultNote: Role-play confident body language and a firm voice. Make sure your child knows who to tell and that they will be believed.

items.subject: martial-arts
items.title: Respect, stance and guard
items.summary: Start with a bow, a balanced stance and a strong guard. Martial arts begin with respect.
steps: Greet your partner or teacher with a bow or fist-in-palm salute.
Stand side-on, feet shoulder-width apart, knees soft.
Hands up by your cheeks, elbows in: this is your guard.
Step forward, back and sideways without crossing your feet.
Balance game: stand on one leg in your stance for 10 seconds.
Finish with a bow. Say thank you.

safety.notes: Adult supervision. Clear space, no contact with others. Bare feet on a non-slip floor.

basic.description: Practise stance, guard and footwork at home.

materials: chalk or tape for floor lines
better.description: Use floor lines for footwork drills.

advanced.description: Join a beginners' class with a qualified coach.

substitutions.use: a carpet or folded blankets on a flat floor

items.subject: martial-arts
items.title: Pad work: jab and cross
items.summary: Practise controlled punches on a pad held by an adult. Technique and control come before power.
steps: Warm up: jog on the spot, arm circles.
From your guard, jab with the front hand, then bring it back to your face.
Cross with the back hand, turning the back foot.
Strike only the pad, never a person.
Breathe out with each strike. Keep it controlled.
Do 3 rounds of 1 minute with rests. Cool down and stretch.

safety.notes: An adult holds the pad and calls stop. Light, controlled strikes. Never strike people. Stop if anything hurts. Outside training, walking away and getting help always comes first.

better.description: Use proper focus pads and wraps.

items.subject: martial-arts
items.title: Combinations, footwork and defence
items.summary: Link strikes into combinations, move with good footwork and practise blocks and slips with a partner.
steps: Warm up and stretch.
Shadow box: jab, cross, step out. Stay balanced.
Pad combinations: jab-cross-hook, then step back.
Defence drills at slow speed: parry, block, slip. No contact to the head.
Conditioning: skipping, squats, planks.
Cool down. Talk about respect and control.

safety.notes: Adult supervision. Slow, no-contact partner drills only. Any contact training belongs at a club with a qualified coach. These are fitness skills: outside training, walking away and getting help always comes first, and never street fighting.

items.subject: martial-arts
items.title: Supervised training and controlled sparring
items.summary: Structured training, strategy and light, controlled sparring, only at a club with qualified supervision.
steps: Train only at a club with a qualified, safeguarding-checked coach.
Wear the required protective gear: gloves, mouthguard, headguard, shin guards.
Agree rules and intensity before every round. Light contact only.
Learn strategy: distance, timing, staying calm.
Stop immediately when the coach or your partner says stop.
Never use these skills outside training. In real danger, walk away, get to a safe place and get help; use force only if there is no other way to escape.

safety.notes: Sparring only with qualified supervision, protective equipment and age-appropriate rules. Never at home. Never street fighting.

items.subject: fitness
items.title: Stretch and move
items.summary: Gentle stretches and mobility moves keep your body flexible.
steps: Warm up first with marching or jogging on the spot.
Neck: slow look left and right.
Arm circles forward and back.
Hamstrings: sit, legs out, reach gently towards toes.
Hold each stretch about 15 to 30 seconds. Breathe slowly.
Stretch gently: it should feel like a pull, never pain.

safety.notes: No bouncing. Stop if anything hurts.

better.description: Use a towel for gentle assisted stretches.

items.subject: fitness
items.title: Bodyweight circuit
items.summary: Squats, wall push-ups, planks and star jumps to build strength and stamina.
steps: Warm up for 3 minutes.
Squats: feet hip-width, sit back, chest up. 10 times.
Wall or knee push-ups: body straight. 8 times.
Plank: forearms and toes (or knees), body straight. 20 seconds.
Star jumps: 20.
Rest 1 minute. Repeat 2 to 3 times. Cool down and stretch.

safety.notes: Good form before more repetitions. Stop if anything hurts. Drink water.

better.description: Do it outdoors using benches for step-ups.

items.subject: fitness
items.title: Posture check
items.summary: Good posture helps your back and neck, especially when studying or using screens.
steps: Stand tall: ears over shoulders, shoulders over hips.
At a desk: feet flat, back supported, screen at eye level.
Every 30 minutes, stand up and move for a few minutes.
Shoulder rolls and chin tucks, 10 each.
Carry your bag on both shoulders.
Photograph your sitting set-up and improve one thing.

hazards: neck or back strain from forcing a position
safety.notes: Gentle movements only.

items.subject: fitness
items.title: Starting resistance training
items.summary: Learn safe technique with bodyweight and light resistance before using heavier weights.
steps: Learn technique with bodyweight first: squat, lunge, push-up, row, hinge.
Add light resistance: water bottles, a backpack with books, or resistance bands.
Do 2 to 3 sets of 8 to 15 controlled repetitions.
Train major muscle groups 2 to 3 days a week, with rest days.
Increase load slowly, only when technique stays good.
Gym machines and barbells: get instruction from a qualified coach first.

safety.notes: Technique first. Adult supervision or a qualified coach for weights. Never train to pain. No maximal lifts without coaching.

🪑 Take breaks from sitting.
🖍️ Colour a box on a chart for each active day.
🎉 After 30 days, celebrate!

safety.notes: Drink water, rest when tired, and choose activities that suit your body.

items.subject: cycling
items.title: Helmet fit and bike check
items.summary: Check your helmet fits and your bike is safe before every ride.
steps: Helmet: sits level, two fingers above eyebrows, straps make a V under the ears, one finger under the chin strap.
Air: squeeze the tyres. They should be firm.
Brakes: squeeze both. The wheels should not turn.
Chain: clean and not loose.
Lights and reflectors if riding in low light.
Bright clothes help others see you.

safety.notes: Keep fingers away from chain and spokes. An adult checks brakes too.

basic.description: Do the checks by hand.

better.description: Pump tyres and oil the chain with an adult.

advanced.description: Add lights and reflective gear.

substitutions.use: bright light-coloured clothing with reflective tape

items.subject: cycling
items.title: Road skills for cyclists
items.summary: Learn to look, signal and ride safely on quiet roads with an adult.
steps: Practise in a car-free area first: riding in a straight line, one-hand signalling, looking over your shoulder.
Learn your local road rules and which side of the road to ride on.
Before moving off or turning: look, signal, look again.
Ride a safe distance from the kerb and parked car doors.
Stop at junctions and wait until it is clear.
Ride on quiet roads with an adult before riding alone. Consider a national cycle training course.

safety.notes: Helmet and bright clothes. Adult accompanies on roads until the child is assessed as ready. Follow local laws.

basic.description: Practise skills in a park or empty playground.

better.description: Ride a short quiet route with an adult.

advanced.description: Take accredited cycle training where offered.

substitutions.use: an experienced adult rider guiding on quiet roads, following local road rules

items.subject: cycling
items.title: Plan a longer ride
items.summary: Plan a route, pack what you need and build up to longer rides.
steps: Choose a route with cycle paths or quiet roads. Check it on a map.
Tell someone your route and when you will be back.
Pack: water, snack, puncture kit or pump, phone, lights, rain layer.
Do the bike check before you set off.
Ride with a friend or adult. Take breaks.
Increase distance a little each time.

safety.notes: Ride with others. Adult approves the route. Helmet and lights.

basic.description: Plan with a paper map.

better.description: Carry repair tools.

advanced.description: Join a supervised club or community ride.

substitutions.use: a paper map and written directions

items.subject: running
items.title: Run-walk plan
items.summary: Mix running and walking, and build up slowly over weeks.
steps: Warm up with 5 minutes of brisk walking.
Run gently for 1 minute, walk for 1 minute. Repeat 6 to 8 times.
Run at a pace where you can still talk.
Do this 3 times a week, adding a little more running each week.
Cool down with walking and stretches.
Run in safe, well-lit places, with a friend or adult.

safety.notes: Safe routes away from traffic, good shoes if available, water, rest days.

basic.description: Run-walk in a park or field.

better.description: Join a free community run if one exists near you.

advanced.description: Join a junior running club.

substitutions.use: counting steps or using any clock

items.subject: hiking
items.title: Family hike
items.summary: Plan a walk in nature, pack well and stay together.
steps: 🗺️ Pick a route that suits the youngest walker.
☁️ Check the weather and tell someone your plan.
🎒 Pack water, snacks, a warm layer, rain layer, sun hat and a small first-aid kit.
🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Stay together. Younger children walk with a grown-up.
🐦 Take breaks and spot plants, birds and clouds.
🧭 Older walkers: learn to read the map and plan the route.

safety.notes: Adult leads. Stay on paths. Keep away from cliff edges and fast water. Do not approach wild animals.

basic.description: A short walk in a local park.

better.description: A countryside walk with a map.

advanced.description: Join a guided walk or youth outdoor group.

substitutions.use: comfortable trainers or shoes with good grip
a paper map and landmarks
